data.narrative:
Q-CTRL, a Series B quantum computing company that has raised $132M to date, operates within a sector comprising 3 public comparables (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private peers including Quantinuum, IonQ, PsiQuantum, D-Wave Quantum, and SandboxAQ. Valuation analysis is constrained by limited precedent at equivalent stages and valuations within this emerging sector.

The stage-progression method is the applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised of $132M as a baseline proxy and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement yields an implied valuation of $251M. This method rests on the assumption that subsequent-stage value creation in quantum computing follows historical venture patterns, though the sector's early maturity introduces execution risk not fully captured by stage-based multiples alone.

The peer-median approach could not be applied; while 8 same-sector private companies exist, fewer than three satisfy narrow filters for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier comparison. Reliance on all-sector median metrics would introduce unacceptable bias. Analysis therefore rests on a single method. The implied valuation range of $213M–$288M (anchored around the $251M median) reflects +/- 15% sensitivity bounds. Key uncertainties include the applicability of venture-stage multiples to frontier technology, heterogeneity in quantum computing business models, and the absence of validated exit comparables at scale in this market.
